A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EvoTest/J-TTL research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on six Jericho games, component and Evolver-model ablations, learning trajectories, computational costs and a controlled Qwen3-32B actor comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a prompt-structure ablation, an all-Qwen control, five-seed summaries, temperature observations and additional backbone evaluations.

M1.justification: The Actor/Evolver loop, four-part agent configuration, transcript-based updates, UCB selection, Algorithm 1 and master prompt retain the same procedure. Expanded explanations, ablation variants and additional backbone configurations do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate repeated learning on Detective, Library, Zork1, Zork3, Balances and Temple. The added experiments reuse these games, especially the Detective/Zork1/Balances subset; newer backbones do not introduce new tasks or environmental conditions.

E2.justification: The main benchmark retains its comparator set. v2 Table 5 adds the explicitly evaluated Simple Mutation comparator, which replaces the structured Evolver instruction with a generic prompt-improvement instruction, alongside EvoPrompt and existing EvoTest variants.

E3.justification: v2 adds a control using Qwen3-32B for both Actor and Evolver, beyond v1's matched-Actor control, and evaluates GPT-5.1 and Gemini-3-Pro-Preview backbones. The 50-episode, 110-step protocol, preprocessing and metrics remain unchanged. Appendix G.2 newly describes positive-reward-only SFT filtering, contradicting the full-trajectory description retained in Appendix D; an actual implementation change or rerun cannot be established.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends analyses of mechanism and model dependence: structured versus generic prompt evolution in Table 5, the all-Qwen control in Table 6, temperature adaptation in Figure 9/Appendix M, and backbone scaling in Appendix N. Existing component ablations and Library/Detective case studies remain. Figure 9 adds temperature evidence alongside a score trajectory already shown in v1 Figure 3.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without repeated-run counts or dispersion. v2 Appendix F/Table 8 explicitly reports AUC means and standard deviations over five random seeds across the benchmark comparison. This introduces substantial uncertainty reporting, but does not establish an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their values, and v1's Qwen/o3 results survive in v2 Tables 6 and 9. Added results include Simple Mutation AUCs of 0.65/0.07/0.20, an all-Qwen three-game average of 0.35, newer-backbone results and five-seed summaries. Figure 3 changes the prompt, UCB, memory and tool-use ablation trajectories despite retaining Table 3's AUC values.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, learning update, AUC definition, UCB equation and computational-cost derivations remain unchanged. v1 Appendix D becomes v2 Appendix E. Additional explanations of UCB symbols and operation do not introduce new mathematical reasoning, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: J-TTL, gradient-free whole-system evolution, superiority over adaptation baselines and unique wins on Detective and Library. The introduction still states 38% improvement over prompt evolution and 57% over online RL. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix A substantially qualifies applicability: frozen-backbone capability limits, task-specific overfitting and brittle transfer, dependence on a powerful Evolver, and possible local optima. v2 also adds interpretations attributing gains to structured evolution, adaptive temperature and stronger backbones, plus expanded explanations of baseline failures.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement and implementation appendix replace anonymous-review repository instructions with the public GitHub destination already footnoted in v1. This updates access instructions rather than establishing a first code release. Hardware, master prompts and promises to release exact seeds, configurations and hyperparameters otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven cited works, including EvoClinician, Just-in-Time Reinforcement Learning, Zombie Agents and Klong. These are mostly brief citation additions and a future-work reference; the central positioning of whole-system evolution relative to prompt optimization, memory and reflection remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introduction's task explanation and navigation example, clarifies UCB operation, brings an expanded controlled comparison into the main text, and inserts new appendix sections. Publication headers, contact information and acknowledgements also change. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation expands substantially through new ablation, uncertainty and backbone tables, a main-text control table separating Actor and Evolver identities, and the dual-axis temperature figure. Figures 2 and 3 receive clearer labels and revised legends. The original Qwen comparison remains as Table 9, and Figure 9 partly reuses an existing score curve.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked reported across-seed variability, and its matched-Actor comparison still used an o3 Evolver. v2's five-seed summaries and all-Qwen control substantially strengthen the central empirical comparison; the prompt-structure ablation and explicit capability and generalization limits further improve support and scope. These gains outweigh introduced reporting weaknesses: Table 8's Memory average of 0.13 conflicts with its displayed game values, which average about 0.18, and Appendices D and G.2 give contradictory SFT training descriptions.
